paragraphs: A corvette is the smallest ship a navy still calls a warship: fast, shallow enough for coastal water, armed well beyond its size. Most fleets that cannot afford frigates build corvettes instead, which is why the class turns up in patrol, escort and littoral defence work all over the world.

The hull carries 195,838 polygons and 212,656 vertices in quads and tris, with non-overlapping UVs and StemCell certification. This listing is the static version; rigged builds are offered separately, including native rigs prepared for Maya and for Cinema 4D.
At $199 it fits naval simulation and training, defence presentation, film and television, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2025.

The arm is the part of the body people understand least well despite using it constantly. Shoulder, elbow and wrist are three joints of completely different design, and the muscles that drive the hand mostly sit in the forearm rather than the hand itself. A skinless arm makes that visible in a way a textbook diagram does not.
The model holds 44,286 polygons and 44,474 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, showing the muscular system over the bone structure. It is built to CheckMate specification.

At $199 it suits medical education and patient explanation, anatomy reference for artists, physiotherapy and sports science material, and character work that needs correct underlying structure. On sale since 2025.

Duck hunting has its own dress code, and it is not the same as deer hunting. Forest pattern camouflage, a fur trimmed collar against cold water mornings, and a shotgun rather than a rifle, because the target is moving fast and close. This character carries that specific kit rather than generic outdoor gear.
The figure runs 149,082 polygons and 87,565 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs. It is delivered in an A pose, ready for your own rig, and holds CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $199 it works for game characters, hunting and outdoor advertising, sporting goods visualisation, film previsualisation and editorial illustration. On sale since 2023.

The hooded wizard is one of the oldest silhouettes in fantasy, and the crystal staff is what tells you which kind he is: not a scholar with a book but a caster who channels through an object. Hood down over the eyes, robe to the floor, weight on the staff rather than on both feet.

The figure holds 78,282 polygons and 99,766 vertices in quads and tris. UVs are overlapping, which suits the repeated cloth and trim, and the character ships rigged and standing rather than in a neutral pose. Built to CheckMate specification.
At $199 it suits game characters, fantasy film and animation, tabletop and card art, book covers and concept illustration. On sale since 2026.

A single skeleton answers questions about bones. A collection of them answers questions about pose, because the skeleton only makes sense once you see it standing, sitting, walking and reaching. Rigged, they can be moved into whatever position the explanation actually needs.
This is a collection listing rather than a single object: the skeletons come rigged and ready to pose, and it carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.

At $199 for the set it suits medical and biology education, museum and exhibition work, anatomy reference for artists and animators, game and film assets. On sale since 2017, which makes it one of the longer running listings in the library.

The C-130 Hercules has been in production longer than almost any other aircraft, and the H model is the version most air forces actually flew. Japan operates its fleet under the Air Self Defense Force in a distinctive scheme, used for transport, airdrop and disaster relief across the islands.

The airframe carries 314,505 polygons and 336,612 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, and comes rigged. Texturing runs to 22 maps: 3 at 8192x8192, 12 at 4096x4096 and 7 at 2048x2048, which is what the panel detail and markings of a real service aircraft require. Built to CheckMate specification.
At $199 it suits flight simulation, aviation and defence visualisation, documentary and film work, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2026.

A mobile drill rig is a drilling tower that drives itself to the hole. The mast folds down for the road and raises on site, which is what makes exploration and water drilling possible in places where a fixed derrick would never be assembled. The truck underneath is as much a part of the machine as the drill.

The model holds 587,686 polygons and 611,731 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, and comes rigged so the mast and running gear can be posed. This page also carries the orange and blue liveries, and native rigged builds prepared for Cinema 4D and for Maya.
At $199 and built to CheckMate specification, it suits mining and exploration visualisation, construction and equipment marketing, training material, film and game environments. On sale since 2025.

Grass pattern camouflage is for open country: field edges, marsh margins, anywhere the cover is low and vertical rather than broken by trees. Paired with a shotgun and a fur trimmed collar, this figure reads as a modern hunter dressed for exactly that ground rather than for woodland.
The character runs 149,082 polygons and 87,565 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, supplied in an A pose ready for your own rig. It holds CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $199 it suits game characters, hunting and outdoor advertising, sporting goods presentation, film previsualisation and editorial work. On sale since 2023.

Mission control is the room the public associates with spaceflight even though nothing flies there. Rows of consoles facing a wall of screens, every station owning one system, the whole layout built so that a hundred specialists can watch one vehicle at once. It has become shorthand for the entire enterprise.

The scene is heavy by design: 2,793,259 polygons and 2,966,552 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, and 31 texture maps all at 4096x4096, covering consoles, seating, displays and the room itself. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $199 it suits documentary and film sets, space programme visualisation, museum and exhibition work, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2020.

The NATO headquarters in Brussels was designed to be read from the air: interlocking fingers of glass that are meant to suggest clasped hands. Whatever one makes of the metaphor, the building is now the visual identifier for the alliance in news and documentary work, the way a parliament building stands in for a government.
The model holds 734,116 polygons and 995,763 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, covering the building and its distinctive plan. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $199 it suits news and documentary graphics, architectural and urban visualisation, editorial illustration, film backgrounds and educational material. On sale since 2022.

The leg carries the whole body, and its anatomy shows it: the largest muscles in the human body sit here, layered around bones built for load rather than dexterity. Stripped of skin, the difference between the thigh and the calf becomes an argument about function rather than shape.

The model holds 64,743 polygons and 65,022 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, showing the muscular system over the bone structure of the leg and foot. It carries StemCell certification.

At $199 it suits medical education and patient explanation, physiotherapy and sports science, anatomy reference for artists, and character work that needs correct underlying structure. On sale since 2024.

An air ambulance is a hospital that has to fit through a rotor disc. Everything about the aircraft follows from that: the cabin door sized for a stretcher, the winch above it, the high visibility scheme meant to be seen from a road at speed. It is the one helicopter most people are pleased to see overhead.

The model is built at subdivision level, 1,357,719 polygons and 1,390,959 vertices with non-overlapping UVs, and comes rigged so the rotors and gear can be posed or animated. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $199 it suits emergency services visualisation, medical and public safety material, film and television, flight simulation, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2020.

The seated Franklin memorial shows him the way the founders wanted him remembered: not standing in oratory but sitting, older, thinking. It is a marble figure at rest, and the pose does more work than any inscription in explaining what he was known for.
The model holds 84,745 polygons and 84,796 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, capturing the figure and its seat. It is built to CheckMate specification.

At $199 it suits historical and educational visualisation, museum and exhibition work, architectural scenes needing period sculpture, film and television, and editorial illustration. On sale since 2025.

The medium van is the vehicle that actually moves a city: too big for a car park space, too small for a lorry licence, and therefore the default for deliveries, trades and small fleets everywhere. A street scene without them looks wrong, and no single model covers the range of shapes in use.

This is a collection listing rather than one vehicle, supplied rigged so wheels and doors can be posed or animated. It is built to CheckMate specification, and the library carries two further volumes of the set, collection 2 and collection 3, for scenes that need more variety.
At $193 the set suits street and city visualisation, logistics and fleet presentation, advertising and mockup work, game environments, film backgrounds and architectural scenes. On sale since 2026.
